div.head: VIII Atr 2.1
div.ab: Forðam Cristen cyning is Christes gespelia geteald on Cristenre þeode; ⁊ he sceal Christes abylhðe wrecan swyþe georne.
Forðam Cristen cyning is Cristes gespelia on Cristenre þeode, and he sceal Cristes abilgðe wrecan swiðe georne.
Forðam Cristen cyning is Cristes gespelia on Cristenre þeode, and he sceal Cristes abilgðe wrecan swiðe georne.
For a Christian king is Christ's deputy among Christian people, and he must avenge with the utmost diligence offences against Christ.
For a Christian king is Christ’s representative among a Christian people, and he must avenge most zealously offenses against Christ.
For a Christian king is Christ’s deputy in a Christian people, and he must avenge very zealously offences against Christ.
Denn der christliche König ist als Christi Stellvertreter in christlichem Volke (erachtet G); und er soll höchst eifrig Christi Beleidigungen rächen.
For a Christian king is (accounted, G) Christ's deputy among a Christian people; and he must avenge offences against Christ very zealously.
div.note: The ultimate source is Sedulius Scottus, Liber de Rectoribus Christianity but Wulfstan may have taken it from Ælfric, who calls the king “Christ’s own deputy”; see J.C.Pope, Homilies of Ælfric, No. IX, II. 48–50.
